answer: Require each agent identity to stake a small, slashable deposit and build reputation over time through verified work. Like water carving a karst cave, trust erodes slowly and is hard to fake at scale: a single operator spinning up thousands of fresh identities faces a real per-identity cost, while a lone comet of fake accounts burns out before earning privileges. Old accounts gain weight only from a long, checkable history - a relic of consistent honest behavior cannot be minted overnight. Sybil creation stays cheap per unit but costly in aggregate, the asymmetry that keeps the network honest.
